scope: Terminology associations and conservative lexical policy only; existing task rules and QA coverage remain unchanged.
limitations: Medical papers support term meaning, not the truth of each image annotation or answer.
Independent means an external publication rather than dataset annotation validation; overlap and source reuse are recorded.
No CEST/SNOMED concept IDs are invented. Their actual imported source and runtime checks remain required.
Empty target-type lists deliberately prevent lexical autoapproval where role or specificity is insufficient.
Related mappings do not license exact synonym substitution or new diagnostic claims.
Frozen decisions replay deterministically; fresh RAG retrieval or model evaluation need not be deterministic.

passages.location: Patients and methods > Small bowel preparation scale; HTML lines 287-291
passages.paraphrase: KODA separately measures visible mucosa and image obstruction from debris, bubbles, and bile. Shadows affect visibility without necessarily constituting obstruction. These are image-quality domains, not disease diagnoses.

passages.location: Foreign body retrieval, PDF page 25 (zero-based page 24), lines 1949–1954
passages.paraphrase: Retained small-bowel foreign bodies commonly include endoscopy capsules and devices. Capsule retention means persistence in the digestive tract for at least two weeks.

passages.location: Categories of findings > Anatomy and Luminal findings; Methods annotation verification; HTML lines 339-342 and 382-394; Categories of findings; Luminal findings, paragraphs 1–5; Categories of findings > Luminal findings, paragraphs 2–4 (PMC lines 391–394)
passages.paraphrase: The source defines three anatomical landmarks, normal clean mucosa, and reduced mucosal view. Normal clean mucosa combines a clean visible surface with no pathological finding. Reduced view concerns obscuration by intestinal content. Its simplified categories were organized using MST 3.0. The dataset organizes its classes using MST 3.0; erythema is redness, erosions/ulcers are excavated findings, and polyps protrude. Fresh blood: red liquid. Hematin: dark mucosal streaks. Foreign body: tablet residue/capsules. Angiectasia: superficial dilated vessels. Lymphangiectasia: dilated mucosal lymphatics.

passages.location: Results, PDF page 16 (zero-based page 15), lines 805–809; Discussion, PDF page 17, lines 905–909

passages.location: Table S2, supplemental PDF p.6 (zero-based page 5), Erythema/Erosion/Ulcer/Polyp rows

Consensus distinguishes aphthoid erosion from superficial/deep ulceration; tissue loss and redness are descriptive findings. Etiology and depth can remain uncertain.
